name: American University in Bulgaria
summary: Independent, not-for-profit, English-taught liberal-arts university in Blagoevgrad; awards US Bachelor of Arts degrees.

programmes.name: Business Administration
programmes.about: Study management, accounting, finance, marketing and organisational behaviour through a liberal-arts business major.
programmes.overview: The Business Administration major covers management, financial and managerial accounting, marketing, business ethics, corporate finance and organisational behaviour. Students can choose a general track or a concentration, and AUBG connects classroom study with its student entrepreneurship activities and accelerator. The liberal-arts structure allows combination with a second major or relevant minor, such as Computer Science or Entrepreneurship. Graduates pursue roles in finance, marketing, consulting and management, or continue to graduate study.

flagshipSource.title: Business major: university describes its accelerator and national standing

programmes.selectionNote: University-wide first-year review: transcript, essay, recommendation, achievements and interview. SAT/ACT is optional; 31 IB points is a recommendation.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: Study programming, computing theory, software development and systems through an English-taught liberal-arts major.
programmes.overview: Computer Science introduces programming in C++ and Java alongside discrete structures, data structures and computer architecture. Students can extend this foundation through software engineering, UNIX and a senior project, with a choice of general track or computing or software-development concentration. AUBG describes connections to industry speakers, alumni and other universities. Students can combine the major with another discipline and progress toward roles in software development, data science or further computing study.

flagshipSource.title: Computer Science: university describes industry partnerships and national standing

programmes.selectionNote: University-wide first-year review: transcript, essay, recommendation, achievements and interview. SAT/ACT is optional; 31 IB points is a recommendation.

programmes.name: Economics
programmes.about: Examine economic choices and markets using microeconomics, macroeconomics, quantitative methods and econometrics.
programmes.overview: Economics explores how households, businesses, governments and markets make decisions through introductory and intermediate microeconomics and macroeconomics. The curriculum also lists quantitative methods, econometrics, economic dynamics and analysis of economic crises, giving students practice with analytical and statistical approaches. AUBG positions the major as a foundation for postgraduate economics or related study. Professional applications include economic analysis, finance, consulting, public policy and roles in business or the nonprofit sector.

programmes.selectionNote: University-wide first-year review: transcript, essay, recommendation, achievements and interview. SAT/ACT is optional; 31 IB points is a recommendation.

programmes.name: Journalism and Mass Communication
programmes.about: Learn reporting, media writing, digital storytelling, visual communication and the ethical dimensions of mass media.
programmes.overview: Journalism and Mass Communication combines study of media and society with writing for media, visual communication, digital storytelling, law and ethics. The published course list includes photography, digital photojournalism and podcasting, while the university describes storytelling activity through clubs and events. Students may connect the subject to Business Administration or Politics through a second major. Graduates can work in journalism, radio, content production, communications and public relations. This is a US-only accredited major and AUBG requires an additional dual-diploma major.

ib.text: Recommends 31 predicted IB points, including TOK/EE, for a provisional offer; may withdraw it below 31 final points. IB courses can accompany another school qualification. English waivers depend on course and grade.

notes: Students enter one liberal-arts BA route and later declare majors; these four examples are not four separate first-year application routes.
Journalism and Mass Communication is a US-only major and must be combined with a major meeting the Bulgarian dual-diploma requirement.
2027/28 tuition is €7,100 per semester before aid, plus activity fees, a meal deposit and housing; foreign school qualifications also require NACID recognition.
